title: OPTIMIZERS
universal_lens: A mathematical framework unifying optimizer architectures through falsifiable e-processes, extremization tuners, and probabilistic pooling under shared entropy-minimization principles. The joint probability operator $P(A \wedge B) = P(A)P(B) + \rho\sqrt{P(A)(1-P(A))P(B)(1-P(B))}$ unifies discrete event co-occurrence with continuous correlation structures. This algebraic form bridges integer linear programming constraints for lineup optimization and transient arbitrage detection, establishing a foundational kernel for multi-agent state-space valuation.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian inference to calibrate optimizer projections using logOddsPool and extremization-tuner gamma, ensuring conformal predictive validity against market-close baselines via falsifyBind. In GSI, the correlation coefficient $\rho$ is treated as a latent variable inferred via Bayesian hierarchical modeling over historical `games harness` data. Conformal prediction intervals are constructed around the joint probability estimates to quantify epistemic uncertainty in parlay pricing, ensuring robust calibration against closing market lines.
gse_mapping: GSE leverages situational reasoning to transition between game states using SaberSim-style simulators, with state transitions governed by recency-weighted lambda and mmc-contribution ensembles. GSE utilizes these primitives to model real-time situational transitions. The ILP optimizer acts as a constraint-satisfaction engine mapping projected player states to optimal lineup configurations, while the arbitrage scanner continuously evaluates live odds feeds to detect transient pricing discrepancies before state decay.

primitives.name: FalsifyBind E-Process
primitives.verbatim_quote: REPO BUILD-NOTES KEY (repeated per section) The repo already holds the infrastructure to test any of these architectures honestly: - `falsifyBind` (packages/prediction-engine/src/edge-lab/falsify.ts) — e-process kill-test; multiplicity gate + leakage/shuffle/split checks.
primitives.assumptions: Optimizer must pass multiplicity gate and leakage checks to be considered valid.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When m > 1 or l > 0.05, the model fails the e-process test.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state transition validation and GSI's calibration consistency checks.

primitives.name: Extremization Tuner Gamma
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `extremization-tuner` (gamma) — controls sharpening between linear pool (γ→0) and geometric/log pool (γ→1+).
primitives.assumptions: Gamma controls convexity of probability aggregation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As γ → 0, converges to linear pooling; as γ → ∞, converges to extreme value pooling.

layer2.mapping: Derives from GSI's probabilistic pooling kernel and informs GSE's confidence adjustment logic.

primitives.name: Log Odds Pool
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `logOddsPool` — geometric-mean aggregation of probabilities; pairs with extremization-tuner.
primitives.assumptions: Geometric mean ensures robustness to outliers in probability estimates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p_i → 0, logOddsPool approaches zero; when all p_i are equal, result equals p_i.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's geometric pooling kernel and GSE's ensemble weighting mechanism.

primitives.name: MMC Contribution Lambda
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `mmc-contribution` / `recency-weighted lambda` — decomposition and decay mechanisms for ensemble/model-averaging layers.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSI's ensemble averaging kernel and GSE's dynamic model reweighting.

primitives.name: Correlation-Adjusted Joint Probability Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Architecture: Joint probability model P(A ∧ B) = P(A)P(B) + ρ√(P(A)(1-P(A))P(B)(1-P(B))).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(A), P(B): Dimensionless marginal probabilities; \rho: Dimensionless Pearson correlation coefficient between binary outcomes A and B.
primitives.assumptions: Outcomes A and B are modeled as Bernoulli trials; the correlation structure is stationary over the estimation window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when |\rho| approaches the theoretical bounds imposed by marginal probabilities (Fréchet inequalities), or when higher-order dependencies dominate pairwise interactions.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to covariance adjustments in multivariate Gaussian copulas used to model dependent scoring events in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Discrepancy between naive product probability and correlation-adjusted fair-price estimates versus closing market.

primitives.name: Integer Linear Programming Lineup Optimizer
primitives.verbatim_quote: [Verified source.] - Build-this-in-repo: The thesis architecture maps directly to an ILP layer that can be wired to `falsifyBind`: create `BacktestRow` objects from historical lineups' actual scores vs projected scores; test whether the ILP optimizer's chosen lineups consistently beat random / projection-neutral selection on `games harness 1999–2025`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p_i: Dimensionless projected score for entity i; x_i: Binary decision variable; A, b: Constraint matrix and vector defining salary/roster limits.
primitives.assumptions: Projected scores are unbiased estimators of true performance; constraints are strictly enforced without transaction costs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when projection noise exceeds the margin of optimization, or when market efficiency forces projections to align perfectly with salary caps.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the GSE constraint solver that allocates limited computational resources across parallel simulation threads.
layer2.telemetry: Actual scores vs projected scores for optimized lineups over the 1999-2025 games harness.

primitives.name: Transient Arbitrage Detection Engine
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### 2.2 Same-Game Parlay (SGP) engines - Architecture: Books build SGPs from proprietary correlation matrices; sharp bettors reverse-engineer.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: O_k: Decimal odds offered by bookmaker k for mutually exclusive outcomes; dimensionless ratio.
primitives.assumptions: Latency is sufficiently low to execute all legs before price correction; no withdrawal fees or account limits interfere.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses under high-frequency trading environments where cancellation risk and execution slippage exceed the theoretical arbitrage margin.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to detecting negative cycles in a weighted directed graph representing currency exchange or betting market states.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of detected soft-arbs and realized ROI after accounting for simulated transaction costs.

primitives.name: Same-Game Parlay Reverse Engineering
primitives.verbatim_quote: BET-SLIP / PARLAY / ARBITRAGE ENGINES ### 2.1 Parlay calculators with correlation adjustments - Core idea: Standard parlay calculators multiply individual implied probabilities (independent assumption), which overstates true probability when events are positively correlated (same-game parlay, SGP).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: X_i, X_j: Binary outcome indicators for events i and j; \hat{\rho}_{ij}: Estimated correlation coefficient; dimensionless.
primitives.assumptions: The bookmaker's pricing reflects a consistent underlying correlation matrix that can be inverted from observed SGP odds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the bookmaker employs non-linear transformations or dynamic hedging strategies that decouple SGP pricing from static historical correlations.

layer2.mapping: Derives the hidden state parameters of the sportsbook's internal GSE model, allowing GSI to anticipate market movements.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of reverse-engineered \rho compared to empirical co-occurrence from games harness.

primitives.name: Platt / Isotonic Calibration Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### 3.2 Calibration layers (Platt / isotonic) - Finding: Platt (sigmoid) and isotonic (monotonic non-parametric) improve Brier on many tabular datasets, but 2025–2026 literature (arXiv:2601.19944v1) reports they can degrade strong modern boosting models.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Brier Score: dimensionless metric of forecast accuracy; Platt Sigmoid: dimensionless logistic mapping function; Isotonic: monotonic non-parametric transformation.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes base model outputs are biased probabilities requiring monotonic transformation to align with true empirical frequencies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when applied to already well-calibrated strong modern boosting models, leading to degraded performance and increased variance.

layer2.mapping: Maps raw feature-engineering outputs to a calibrated probability simplex, acting as a necessary kernel smoothing step before GSI evaluation.
layer2.telemetry: Brier score improvement on holdout sets; negative delta triggers veto.

primitives.name: Extremization-Tuner Conditional Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Wire `logOddsPool` and `extremization-tuner` together so sharpening only activates when Brier improves.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: logOddsPool: dimensionless log-odds aggregation buffer; extremization-tuner: operator applying sharpening transform; Brier: dimensionless loss metric.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes probability sharpening (extremization) reduces expected log-loss only under specific distributional conditions of the underlying pool.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the logOddsPool contains highly collinear or stale signals, causing the tuner to amplify noise rather than signal.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a conditional expectation operator in GSE that modifies state-transition probabilities only when information gain is positive.
layer2.telemetry: Delta Brier score between raw logOddsPool and tuned output.

primitives.name: Bayesian Hierarchical Team Effects
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Recipe: Model y_ig ~ Binom(p_ig, n) with logit(p_ig) = α_team[i] + β_team[j] + γ_home + ε_ig; priors N(0, σ_team) with σ_team ~ Half-Cauchy(1).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: y_ig: integer game outcome; p_ig: dimensionless win probability; alpha/beta: dimensionless team attack/defense strength; gamma_home: dimensionless home advantage; epsilon_ig: dimensionless game noise; sigma_team: dimensionless hyperparameter scale.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes team strengths are drawn from a global population distribution and exhibit partial pooling; outcomes follow binomial processes conditioned on latent traits.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs with extreme data sparsity (e.g., single-game seasons) where hyperpriors dominate, or severe model misspecification regarding the binomial variance.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSI's core belief-updating engine, providing posterior distributions for team states used in Monte Carlo simulations.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior predictive coverage rates against `falsifyBind` closing-line null.

primitives.name: FalsifyBind Multiplicity Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Build note: Fit hierarchical Stan model to `games harness 1999–2025`; compare posterior predictive distributions to `falsifyBind` closing-line null; if hierarchical model's predictive intervals don't cover outcomes at expected rate, the model fails the falsifiable coverage gate.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: falsifyBind: verification operator; posterior predictive distribution: probability density over outcomes; coverage rate: dimensionless frequency of observed outcomes within confidence intervals.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the closing-line market represents an efficient null hypothesis against which internal model calibration must be tested.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Gate fails if market efficiency assumptions collapse (e.g., massive line movement due to injury news post-close) or if the hierarchical model severely underestimates tail risk.

layer2.mapping: Acts as the final epistemic filter in GSI, rejecting any model whose uncertainty quantification does not align with market-implied probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical coverage frequency vs. nominal confidence level (e.g., 90% interval covers 90% of outcomes).

primitives.name: Covariance-Adjusted Portfolio Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Data: Covariance matrix of bet outcomes (estimated from historical co-occurrence or model simulation); expected-return vector μ.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w': 'portfolio weight vector (dimensionless)', 'μ': 'expected return vector (dimensionless)', 'Σ': 'covariance matrix of bet outcomes (dimensionless)', 'γ': 'risk aversion parameter (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Returns are multivariate normal; Σ and μ are known or estimated with bounded error.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Σ becomes singular or μ is poorly estimated, optimization fails.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian portfolio calibration where μ and Σ are derived from falsified model outputs.
layer2.telemetry: Portfolio Sharpe ratio and out-of-sample performance relative to null model.

primitives.name: Risk-of-Ruin Gambler's Ruin Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: Standard gambler's ruin formula: P(ruin) = (1 - (q/p)^B) / (1 - (q/p)^G) for p ≠ q.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p': 'win probability (dimensionless)', 'q': 'loss probability (dimensionless)', 'B': 'initial bankroll (currency units)', 'G': 'target bankroll (currency units)'}
primitives.assumptions: Fixed win probability p, constant payout b, finite bankroll B, and fixed target G.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p approaches 0.5 or B/G grows large, convergence issues arise.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to simulate sequential betting paths and adjust stake sizes dynamically based on estimated p.
layer2.telemetry: Simulated ruin probability under varying p estimates and model falsification events.

primitives.name: Fractional Staking with Lower Bound Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### 4.4 Fractional sizing under estimation error - Approach: Replace point-estimate p with lower confidence-bound p_lower (e.g., from `falsifyBind` e-process lower bound or from Bayesian posterior lower quantile).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f': 'fractional stake (dimensionless)', 'p_lower': 'lower confidence bound of win probability (dimensionless)', 'q': 'loss probability (dimensionless)', 'b': 'payout ratio (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: p_lower is conservative estimate of true win probability; payout b is fixed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p_lower approaches q, f → 0, leading to no-stake behavior.

layer2.mapping: Applied in GSE to compute safe fractional stakes using lower bounds from `falsifyBind`.
layer2.telemetry: Stake size adjustment ratio and corresponding reduction in volatility.

primitives.name: Multiplicity Gate Failure Detection
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the aggregated predictions fail multiplicity gate, the portfolio is over-confident regardless of Kelly formula.
primitives.assumptions: Aggregated predictions are subject to multiplicity bias; portfolio weights are derived from them.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When multiple correlated models predict same outcome, overconfidence arises.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSI’s use of `falsifyBind` to detect overfitting in prediction ensembles.
layer2.telemetry: Number of falsified models in ensemble and associated confidence penalty.

reasoning_traces.think: The mathematical foundation of this chapter window rests on the transition from independent Bernoulli trials to correlated multivariate distributions. Standard parlays assume independence, effectively setting $\rho=0$, which systematically overstates the joint probability of co-occurring events like a quarterback throwing for 300 yards and a receiver catching for 100. The introduction of the correlation-adjusted joint probability operator provides a rigorous correction, embedding the dependency structure directly into the valuation kernel. This operator is not merely a statistical adjustment but a fundamental component of the Integer Linear Programming (ILP) framework used for lineup optimization. By incorporating accurate joint probabilities, the ILP solver avoids selecting lineups that appear optimal under independence assumptions but suffer from redundant exposure to correlated risks. Furthermore, the detection of transient arbitrage opportunities relies on identifying moments where the market's implicit correlation matrix diverges from the empirically derived one. The 'soft' arb scanner operates as a high-frequency monitor of these divergences, exploiting the lag between true probabilistic reality and market pricing. The verification of these primitives through backtesting on the 1999-2025 games harness ensures that the theoretical gains are not artifacts of overfitting but reflect genuine structural inefficiencies. The reverse engineering of Same-Game Parlay (SGP) engines further solidifies this approach by treating the sportsbook as a black box whose internal correlation parameters can be estimated and exploited. Ultimately, the unification of ILP optimization, correlation adjustment, and arbitrage detection creates a cohesive system for extracting value from complex, interdependent sporting events.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This lineage traces back to early 20th-century probability theory, specifically the work of Karl Pearson on correlation coefficients and the development of multivariate normal distributions. In sports analytics, it evolved from simple regression models in the 1970s to sophisticated Monte Carlo simulations in the 1990s. The advent of high-frequency data and computational power enabled the shift from aggregate team statistics to granular player-level correlation matrices, culminating in modern SGP engines and automated arbitrage scanners that operate in real-time.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires understanding that sportsbooks are not passive price-takers but active participants employing their own proprietary correlation matrices and risk management algorithms. Sharp bettors must anticipate how the bookmaker adjusts lines in response to large bets, effectively playing a game of chicken where both sides try to predict the other's reaction function. The reverse engineering of SGP engines is essentially a mind-reading exercise, inferring the bookmaker's internal state from observable pricing anomalies. This adversarial dynamic necessitates constant adaptation, as any successful strategy will eventually be incorporated into the bookmaker's model, eroding its edge.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity vetoes are crucial to prevent leakage between the ILP optimizer and the arbitrage scanner. If the optimizer consistently selects players based on a flawed correlation assumption, it may inadvertently create artificial arbitrage opportunities that vanish upon execution. Similarly, the arbitrage scanner must not rely on the same historical window as the correlation estimator to avoid look-ahead bias. Strict separation of training and testing sets, along with rigorous cross-validation, ensures that the primitives remain robust and do not degrade due to overfitting or circular reasoning. The veto condition triggers if the discrepancy between projected and actual performance exceeds a predefined threshold, indicating a breakdown in the underlying assumptions.

reasoning_traces.think:
The chapter window delineates a rigorous pipeline for transforming raw sports data into verifiable probabilistic edges. It begins by acknowledging that feature engineering alone is insufficient; without calibration, models lack verifiable edge. The introduction of Platt and isotonic calibration layers serves as a mathematical projection, forcing raw model outputs onto a manifold where predicted probabilities align with empirical frequencies. However, the text astutely notes that this is not a free lunch—modern boosting models may already be well-calibrated, and forcing a sigmoid or isotonic transform can degrade performance. This necessitates the `extremization-tuner`, a conditional operator that only sharpens probabilities if it demonstrably improves the Brier score. 

Simultaneously, the window introduces Bayesian hierarchical models as a foundational primitive for capturing team dynamics. By modeling team strengths as random effects drawn from a global distribution (with Half-Cauchy priors), the model achieves partial pooling, effectively regularizing estimates for teams with sparse data. This hierarchical structure provides not just point estimates, but full posterior distributions, enabling robust uncertainty quantification. The ultimate test of this entire framework is the `falsifyBind` multiplicity gate. This gate compares the hierarchical model's posterior predictive intervals against the closing-line market odds. If the model's uncertainty estimates do not cover actual outcomes at the expected rate, the model is rejected. This creates a closed-loop system where mathematical rigor (Bayesian inference) is continuously validated against market efficiency (closing lines), ensuring that only truly calibrated, non-degenerate edges are deployed.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This lineage traces back to early 20th-century statistical mechanics and the development of maximum entropy principles. The use of hierarchical Bayes echoes Gelman and Hill's work on multilevel modeling, adapting social science techniques to sports analytics. The `extremization-tuner` reflects a modern evolution of Platt scaling, responding to the overconfidence often seen in deep ensembles. The `falsifyBind` gate inherits from the efficient market hypothesis, treating closing lines as the ultimate ground truth for probability calibration.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires understanding that coaches and players adapt to perceived weaknesses. The hierarchical model captures this by treating team strength as a dynamic latent variable influenced by recent performance and opponent quality. The `logOddsPool` aggregates market sentiment, which itself is a collective theory-of-mind construct reflecting public and sharp money expectations. By wiring the tuner to only activate when Brier improves, the system avoids overreacting to noise, mirroring a disciplined agent that ignores fleeting market irrationality unless it presents a statistically significant opportunity.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by the `falsifyBind` gate, which vetoes any model whose predictive intervals fail to cover outcomes at the expected rate. This prevents leakage from overfitted features that might artificially inflate short-term Brier scores but fail out-of-sample validation. The conditional nature of the `extremization-tuner` also acts as a veto, disabling sharpening if it degrades calibration. Furthermore, the hierarchical priors inherently veto extreme parameter estimates by shrinking them toward the global mean, ensuring that no single anomalous game disproportionately influences long-term team strength estimates.
